about: Where the sun is in the rendered images of the three.js original (oracle-4112f57-h8) and the Godot port, measured from pixels: tools/sun_locate.gd (port buffers and --analyze), tools/sun_locate_gpu.gd (GLSL compute), tools/sun_locate_fit.gd, tools/oracle/sun_cams.mjs (the original's live cameras and sun). Azimuth is the shadow's direction atan2(-Lz, -Lx) in degrees, elevation asin(Ly), L pointing at the sun.
verdict: Same sun. Both images put the sun within 0.5 deg of SUN_DIR and of each other, by the post shadows and, independently, by the toon bands; the 2 deg control is detected and fails the gate, and the original measured twice agrees with itself. No axis flip, sign slip or wrong vector: the remaining shadow differences belong to the shadow-map setup (see shadow_setup).

shadow_setup.original: PCFSoftShadowMap (shadowMap.type 2, three r170): a fixed 3x3 bilinear-weighted kernel, about a 4-texel footprint
shadow_setup.port: PCF, soft_shadow_filter_quality 2 (Soft Low: 4 Vogel taps, radius blur 1.0 x 2 texels), light_angular_distance 0.0 (no PCSS)
shadow_setup.effect: edge softness: the original's edges blur over about 1.5 texels a side; the port's PCF is thresholded by MToon (below), so its edges stay hard

shadow_setup.original: shadow.radius 1.6: ignored, three r170 reads radius only for PCFShadowMap and VSM
shadow_setup.effect: none in the original; porting radius 1.6 as a blur would soften the port beyond the original

shadow_setup.port: directional atlas 4096 (16-bit depth: true), 4 splits of 2048 each

shadow_setup.original: orthographic box +-75 m (quality.shadowSize at high), near 1, far 520; target = camera + 0.45 S ahead (horizontal), snapped to texels in light space; light 260 m up the sun
shadow_setup.port: PSSM 4 splits to 100 m (max distance), offsets 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5 -> far 10.09 / 20.08 / 50.05 / 100 m view depth; each split's box fits its frustum slice's bounding sphere, snapped (stable); pancake 20 m; fade from 80 %; blend_splits false
shadow_setup.effect: the port has no shadow past 100.00 m (about 1515 soda cans) of view depth (fading from 80 %); the original has none outside its box; the port's quality steps at the split seams

shadow_setup.port: 1.2 cm (about 1.2 AAA batterys) / 2.3 cm (about 1.1 nickels) / 5.7 cm (about 1.0 adult wrist) / 11.3 cm (about 1.7 soda cans) by split (this camera: 58 deg, 16:9)
shadow_setup.effect: the port is sharper than the original inside 20 m of view depth and coarser beyond; a bollard is 3 of the original's texels wide, so thin posts rasterize coarsely there

shadow_setup.original: bias -0.00035 in [0,1] depth over far - near = 519 m: 18.2 cm (about 2.8 soda cans) toward the light
shadow_setup.port: shadow_bias 0.10: 0.10 / 100 x (2 r + pancake) x blur x quality radius -> 9.0 cm (about 1.4 soda cans) (split 1) to 13.3 cm (about 2.0 soda cans) (split 2) toward the light
shadow_setup.effect: removes shadow where the occluder is that close along the ray: a lit gap at the foot of each post, largest in the original

shadow_setup.original: normalBias 3.5 cm (about 1.7 nickels) along the world normal: on the paving the lookup moves 5.8 cm (about 1.0 adult wrist) away from the sun, and tips shorten by that
shadow_setup.port: shadow_normal_bias 2.0 x split texel along the normal, its part along the light removed: 2.4 cm (about 1.1 nickels) / 4.5 cm (about 1.1 golf balls) / 11.4 cm (about 1.7 soda cans), so tips shorten 4.0 cm (about 1.9 nickels) / 7.5 cm (about 1.1 soda cans) / 19.0 cm (about 2.9 soda cans) by split
shadow_setup.effect: shadows shorter toward the sun by b / tan(elevation); in the port the shortening jumps at each split seam

shadow_setup.original: MeshToonMaterial: sun irradiance x shadow (linear), so the visible edge sits at 50 % attenuation; in shadow only the hemisphere light remains (about 23 % of lit luminance on the paving, then graded blue-violet)
shadow_setup.port: MToon: the attenuation enters lightIntensity before the toon ramp (_ShadeToony 0.9, _ShadeShift 0), so the edge snaps at about 69 % attenuation (paving, N.L 0.52); in shadow the shade colour (0.72, 0.68, 0.82) stays lit by the sun (42 % of lit in the sun alone)
shadow_setup.effect: the port's shadows are harder, slightly larger (dilated) and lighter than the original's

shadow_setup.setting: edge model fitted to the images (light plane)
shadow_setup.original: dilation 8.2 mm (about 1.2 pencils), normal-bias shift 5.7 cm (about 1.0 adult wrist), blur 2.5 cm (about 1.2 nickels)
shadow_setup.port: dilation 0.327 texel, normal-bias shift 1.807 texel (setting 2.0), blur 3.3 mm (about 2.2 pennys)
shadow_setup.effect: measured, not assumed: the sun is fitted with these as free parameters, so they do not bias it

moge.why: RFD 2294 (where compute runs): heavy compute runs in a godot-sandbox guest or on ggml-rd/compute-rd, never as a host Python pipeline, and MoGe may run only as ggml in a guest; RFD 1167 lists MoGe read-only with no ggml-rd port, so method B would need that port first
moge.cost_of_the_python_route_not_taken: a host deep-learning framework with GPU wheels (about 3 GB), MoGe's helper packages, a GPU kernel compiler for MoGe-3, and the 1.3 GB checkpoint; about 10 minutes on this desk, and off the route
moge.cost_of_the_allowed_route: a ggml port of DINOv2-L (24 ViT blocks) plus MoGe-2's conv heads into a guest on ggml-rd, then 8 oracle views at its 1.3 GB weights: a project of its own
moge.would_add: normals and depth independent of the port's geometry, a check of the cameras; here the cameras are checked directly instead (cameras: the original's live matrices against the port's, and its own depth against the port's)
